feedback: The RM correctly captures the task 'turn the siren off every time it rings'. Semantic fidelity: siren_ringing is a persistent condition, and the transition (u0,siren_ringing)->u1 uses it as a trigger per episode-ring, which is appropriate; switch_toggled & !siren_ringing correctly marks the silencing toggle (since the siren stops only via the switch toggle). Reachability: u1 is reachable on every seed because the first ring occurs within the first 30 steps; u2 is reachable since the siren stays on until toggled, so the guard eventually holds. Compactness: three states is minimal for repeated rings (u2 allows new rings to re-enter u1, covering subsequent rings). Ordered transition coverage: each state has an explicit else self-loop, so irrelevant events (client_arrived, order_taken, food_prepared, order_served, food_fell, served_while_ringing, holding_food) are absorbed correctly. Predicate-only events: the guard switch_toggled & !siren_ringing is well formed; the next-ring condition in u2 uses siren_ringing alone, which cannot co-occur with switch_toggled stopping it. Persistent/event distinction: siren_ringing used as entry (rising edge effectively, since it can only be true after being false in u0/u2), and switch_toggled with the complement guard distinguishes a silencing toggle from a meaningless silent toggle. Reward: dense enough for the task, bounded (+0.1 progress, +1.0 completion), no unsafe large or negative rewards; no reward on u2 self-loop, avoiding reward farming. Regressions handled explicitly via (u2, siren_ringing)->u1 for the next ring. Header check: FINAL_STATES u2 is nonempty and declared as a state; accepting u2 is appropriate since no further requirement exists there. Minor note (non-blocking): the +0.1 on entering u1 gives a small penalty-like signal of an unhandled ring, which is a reasonable shaping choice; no changes required.
